messages:
Olivia Chen: hey @eng-platform — saw a weird jump in the consolidated latency dashboard for p95 around 14:03 UTC, but when I break it down by endpoint the same timeslice looks flat. wondering if this is a sampling/rollup artifact or a frontend calc mismatch :thinking:

Raj Patel: can you paste the dashboard link and the exact metric id? my first guess is tdigest merge skew when routes with very different sample counts are combined.

Olivia Chen: https://console.redwood/metrics/dash/AA12 -> metric: latency_ms.tdigest.pctl, endpoint=api.v1.generate
snapshot: p50=120, p95=420, p99=1020 at 14:03; endpoint breakdown shows p95 ~150 across all endpoints.

Raj Patel: ok. two quick checks: 1) sample_count for the rollup at that rollup window, 2) whether the frontend sparkline is recomputing percentiles client-side from batched histograms vs using the precomputed pctl. run a quick query like: 
```
SELECT sum(sample_count) as cnt, approx_percentile(hist, 50,95,99) as p FROM metrics.rollups
WHERE metric='latency_ms' AND rollup_window='15m' AND ts >= 2832104400 AND endpoint='api.v1.generate'
```

Marta Lopez: UI note — our sparkline panel is intentionally lightweight and shows "instant" percentiles from last 1m window; the Pctl table uses 15m rollups for stability. That mismatch has bitten us before. We should show the window in the card header.

observability-bot: alert: metric anomaly detected: latency_ms.tdigest.pctl p95 spike (14:03) in rollup id rr-33. Link: https://console.redwood/alerts/rr-33 :rotating_light:

Kai Nguyen: also remember our rollup merge_mode is "weighted_by_count" by default, but if one route suddenly drops samples (e.g., traffic routed away) tdigest merge can produce non-monotonic percentiles. We added a heuristic in prod to fallback to raw histogram if merged_count < 50.

Ben Ortiz: could the routing change yesterday (canary for dynamic-model-routing) cause a short-lived mix of model variants with different latencies? If one variant got a handful of large-latency tails, the global p95 could spike while per-endpoint looks steady because the variant tag isn't surfaced in that breakdown.

Olivia Chen: hmm we don't tag by model_variant on that dashboard. I'll re-run with route + variant tags.

Raj Patel: if you find low sample counts, try re-running the rollup calculation with merge_mode: "preserve-per-route" (i.e., compute percentiles per-route then aggregate medians) or switch to raw histogram-based percentiles for that window. Example config snippet: 
```
rollup_policy:
  method: tdigest
  window: 15m
  merge_mode: weighted_by_count  # alternatives: preserve-per-route, raw-histogram-fallback
  min_merge_count: 50
```

Marta Lopez: UX follow-up: proposal to add small 'sample count' micro-rows under each percentile in the table (p50/p95/p99 — count: N). Also an inline tooltip explaining tdigest merge caveats.

Olivia Chen: +1. For immediate troubleshooting I ran the sample-count query — total_count=38 at that window for the merged metric. so that explains it.

Kai Nguyen: yeah count < 50 => tdigest merge unreliable. We should tweak the alert to include "merged_count < threshold" so SLO noise reduces.

sre-bot: deploy queued: observability/backend@v2.4.1 includes min_merge_count param (defaults to 100) and sample_count expose on UI. PR: https://git.internal/r/4567

Ben Ortiz: nice. One more ops thing: if we start exposing sample_count everywhere, we should also surface routing weights so root-cause isn't hidden (e.g., route=A 90%, route=B 10%).

Olivia Chen: thanks all — will retag dashboard with model_variant, add sample_count column, and follow up on the UX doc. filing a tiny follow-up ticket in eng-platform board. :thumbsup:

Raj Patel: thanks — this is classic tdigest vs small-n problem. good catch! :eyes:
